metadata.description: AST fixture for the flux-form first-order-upwind MERIDIONAL advection rule -- the tracer half of the meridional CWC transport pair. Carries BOTH a cell-centred tracer and a face-staggered meridional wind, and BOTH the compound flux-form rule and the plain-D lat rule, so the golden pins that the esm-spec 9.6.3 outermost-first precedence plus the 9.6.1 shape constraint route each derivative to its own rule with no ambiguity and no priority race.
metadata.name: latlon3d_upwind1_flux_D_lat_polar

coslat.description: Metric factor cos(lat_j) over the lat index set: the cosine of lat_coord converted to radians inside (pi/180 with pi = 3.141592653589793). Used by consumers composing physical-units zonal derivatives, df/dx_east = (180/pi) D(f, lon) / (R_sphere * coslat) — see metadata.description. Inherits lat_coord's free names lat0_deg and dlat_deg.

coslat_edge.description: FACE-LENGTH metric over the lat_nodes (NLAT+1 face) axis: coslat_edge[gjc] = cos(pi/180 * phie[gjc]), where phie is the consumer's degree-valued edge array (shape [lat_nodes], from lat_edge). This is the zonal length of the latitude face, in units of R dlon_rad. On the global recipe the two POLE faces have coslat_edge = cos(-/+pi/2) = 6.1e-17 in IEEE double, NOT 0 — which is precisely why the flux-form lat rules OMIT the pole-wall flux terms rather than multiplying them by this near-zero factor (see metadata.description). Aggregate index `gjc`, distinct from the producer's `gje` and from its sibling consumers' `gja`/`gjd` (hygiene; see metadata.description).

deg2rad.description: Degree-to-radian helper: angle_deg * pi/180 (pi = 3.141592653589793). Invoke with any scalar or array expression binding; pure sugar for metric-factor compositions.

lat_coord.description: Point latitudes lat_j = lat0_deg + (j - 1) dlat_deg (degrees), shaped over the lat index set (endpoint-inclusive; the global recipe runs pole to pole). lat0_deg and dlat_deg are free names supplied by the consuming model (see metadata.description).

lat_edge.description: Latitude CELL EDGES in DEGREES, over the lat_nodes (NLAT+1 face) axis: phie[gje] = max(lat0_deg, min(latN_deg, lat0_deg + (gje - 1.5) dlat_deg)), latN_deg = lat0_deg + (NLAT - 1) dlat_deg. Each interior edge is the midpoint of the two neighbouring lat POINTS; the two end edges CLAMP to the domain ends, which halves the two end cells and so reproduces GEOS-Chem's half-polar caps on the global recipe (see metadata.description). Branch-free (min/max, no ifelse). Face gje is the LOWER (southern) edge of cell gje. Assumes dlat_deg > 0. Takes no arguments: it folds from the free names lat0_deg and dlat_deg plus the NLAT metaparameter. THE CONSUMER declares an observed `phie` of shape [lat_nodes] by applying this template, then feeds that same `phie` to coslat_edge / latcell_area / latcell_dphi — the keyed-factor contract grids/latlon3d uses for pe -> lev_thickness. This is the PRODUCER template, and its aggregate index `gje` is deliberately DISTINCT from the consumers' (gjc/gja/gjd): non-hygienic inlining would otherwise let a consumer's offset gather phie[gj+1] be captured by this body's own index and silently lose the +1 (see the AGGREGATE-INDEX HYGIENE paragraph in metadata.description).

latcell_area.description: EXACT spherical cell-area weight over the lat (cell) axis: latcell_area[gja] = sin(pi/180 * phie[gja+1]) - sin(pi/180 * phie[gja]), gathering the consumer's NLAT+1-node degree-valued edge array phie. This is the exact integral of cos(phi) dphi across the cell, not a midpoint approximation, so the flux-form meridional divergence (F[j+1] coslat_edge[j+1] - F[j] coslat_edge[j]) / latcell_area[j] telescopes to an exact global mass budget. Positive when dlat_deg > 0. The physical cell area on a sphere of radius R is R^2 dlon_rad latcell_area[gja]. At the two half-polar caps latcell_area ~ dphi^2/8 — SECOND order small in the grid spacing while the adjacent face is only FIRST order small (coslat_edge ~ dphi/2); that O(1/dphi) amplification is why near-pole convergence requires the product V dq/dphi to vanish like cos(phi) at the pole (see grids/latlon3d/rules/upwind1_flux_D_lat_polar). Aggregate index `gja`, distinct from the producer's `gje` — with a shared name the offset gather phie[gja+1] is captured and silently degenerates to phie[gja], returning EXACT ZEROS (see the AGGREGATE-INDEX HYGIENE paragraph in metadata.description).

latcell_dphi.description: Cell angular WIDTH in RADIANS over the lat (cell) axis: latcell_dphi[gjd] = pi/180 * (phie[gjd+1] - phie[gjd]), gathering the consumer's NLAT+1-node degree-valued edge array phie. Interior cells are a full dlat_deg wide; the two end (polar-cap) cells are HALF that, a direct consequence of the lat_edge clamp. The physical north-south cell width on a sphere of radius R is R latcell_dphi[gjd]. Needed by the ZONAL flux-form operator (which weights the zonal divergence by the cell width) and by any consumer wanting the meridional spacing; the MERIDIONAL flux-form operator does NOT need it, since latcell_area already carries the exact area weight. Aggregate index `gjd`, distinct from the producer's `gje` for the offset-gather hygiene reason in metadata.description.

lev_center.description: Cell (level) centers from the edge array: lev_center[gk] = (pe[gk] + pe[gk+1]) / 2 over the lev (cell) axis, gathering the NLEV+1-node edge array pe (shape [lev_nodes]). A consuming model applies this to its `pe` to define its lev-shaped `zc` observed. The aggregation index is `gk`, NOT `k`, so the derived observed does not capture a consuming vertical stencil's own aggregate index `k` when inlined (the non-hygienic-inlining footgun; see grids/cartesian_nonuniform_1d/nonuniform_cell_center).

lev_thickness.description: Finite-volume control thicknesses from the edge array: lev_thickness[gk] = pe[gk+1] - pe[gk] over the lev (cell) axis. A consuming model applies this to its `pe` to define its lev-shaped `dp` observed (positive when pe is monotone increasing with the lev index — the required orientation). Aggregation index `gk` (distinct from a rule's `k`) for the same hygiene reason as lev_center.

lev_thickness_3d.description: TERRAIN-FOLLOWING (rank-3) control thicknesses from a THREE-DIMENSIONAL edge array: lev_thickness_3d[gi,gj,gk] = pe[gi,gj,gk+1] - pe[gi,gj,gk] over [lon, lat, lev], gathering the [lon, lat, lev_nodes] edge array pe. This is the Psurf-coupled hybrid-sigma-pressure counterpart of lev_thickness: a consuming model builds a 3-D pressure-at-edges pe[i,j,kn] = Ap[kn] + Bp[kn]*Ps(i,j,t) (which varies in longitude, latitude and time whenever the surface pressure does) and applies this template to define its [lon,lat,lev]-shaped `dp` observed (positive when pe increases with the lev index — the required orientation). The physical `dp` is the reconstruction width consumed by the terrain-following flux-form vertical operators (ppm_flux_D_lev_mono_hybrid_noflux_bc). Aggregation indices gi/gj/gk (distinct from a rule's i/j/k) for the non-hygienic-inlining reason documented on lev_center and lev_thickness.

lon_coord.description: Cell-center longitudes lon_i = lon0_deg + (i - 1/2) dlon_deg (degrees), shaped over the lon index set. lon0_deg and dlon_deg are free names supplied by the consuming model (see metadata.description for the contract and the global recipe).

V.description: Face-staggered MERIDIONAL wind on the NLAT+1 face axis, positive northward: V = coslat_e[j] a(i) b(k), a wind that vanishes at the poles like cos(phi). It is the lat_nodes index-set NAME in this declared shape -- not its size -- that lets the rule's `where` constraint tell the face wind apart from the cell tracer u.

coslat_e.description: FACE-LENGTH weight cos(phi_e), from the grid's coslat_edge template (aggregate index `gjc`, deliberately distinct from the producer's `gje`). The golden pins that the OFFSET GATHER coslat_e[j+1] inside the operator survives inlining with its offset intact -- a colliding aggregate index would silently degenerate it to coslat_e[j] and return exact zeros.

dS_lat.description: EXACT spherical cell-AREA weight sin(phi_e[j+1]) - sin(phi_e[j]), from the grid's latcell_area template (aggregate index `gja`). Its own offset gather phie[gja+1] is likewise pinned by the golden.

dlat_deg.description: 180/(NLAT-1) = 36 for NLAT = 6, spelled as a LITERAL: every metaparameter is pinned at the import edge of an AST fixture, so NLAT is consumed there and is not live in this document's runtime scope (esm-spec 9.7.6). Read by lat_edge and by central_D_lat_zero_grad_bc.

lat0_deg.description: Southern domain edge; the grid's lat0_deg free name. -90 with dlat_deg = 36 and NLAT = 6 is the GLOBAL pole-to-pole recipe, whose end cells are the half-polar caps: phie = [-90, -72, -36, 0, 36, 72, 90].

phie.description: Latitude cell EDGES in degrees over the NLAT+1 face axis, from the grid's lat_edge template (aggregate index `gje`). The golden pins the clamped-midpoint recipe max(lat0, min(latN, lat0 + (gje - 3/2) dlat)) -- branch-free min/max, no ifelse -- and hence the half-polar caps.
